claim_classes.name: STRUCTURAL / PROTOCOL CLAIM
claim_classes.definition: Claim about specification identity, control routing, protocol completeness, status preservation, reconstructibility, or authority boundaries, without asserting market behavior, predictive performance, profitability, OOS evidence, or historical tradability.
examples: The pre-result manifest was frozen before result exposure.
The same canonical inputs reconstruct the same control graph.
Owner-native BLOCKED was preserved rather than converted to FAIL.

claim_classes.name: DESCRIPTIVE MARKET-BEHAVIOR CLAIM
claim_classes.definition: Retrospective description of observed market-data properties or empirical distributions without asserting that the information was historically available for a trading decision or that a predictive/economic edge exists.
examples: Observed returns in the declared dataset have this empirical quantile profile.
Observed spread distribution differs across declared windows.

claim_classes.name: STATISTICAL EFFECT CLAIM
claim_classes.definition: Inferential claim that a declared effect, association, difference, or estimand is supported beyond descriptive reporting within an explicitly declared validity scope.
examples: The declared effect is distinguishable from the preregistered null under dependence-aware inference.
The estimated effect clears the minimum-effect threshold with qualified uncertainty.
forbidden_escalations: effect estimate -> causal effect unless causation is separately established

claim_classes.name: PREDICTIVE CLAIM
claim_classes.definition: Claim that information available under the declared temporal model predicts a future target under a frozen prediction protocol.
examples: The frozen model predicts the declared future target above the preregistered baseline.
A probabilistic forecast is calibrated within the declared evaluation surface.
forbidden_escalations: post-hoc feature availability -> historical predictive validity

claim_classes.name: ECONOMIC / NET-PROFITABILITY CLAIM
claim_classes.definition: Claim about economically material net outcomes after the execution and cost semantics required by the declared trading policy.
examples: Net expectancy remains above the preregistered minimum after all claim-required costs.
The frozen strategy remains economically viable under the declared execution model.

claim_classes.name: ROBUSTNESS / STABILITY CLAIM
claim_classes.definition: Claim that a previously declared effect or behavior remains materially stable across preregistered parameter, temporal, regime, perturbation, or influence checks.
examples: The effect survives the preregistered regime partitions.
The conclusion is not driven by a small set of influential observations.

claim_classes.name: MULTIPLICITY / MODEL-SELECTION CLAIM
claim_classes.definition: Claim about evidence after accounting for declared search exposure, multiple hypotheses, model selection, or data-snooping risk.
examples: The family-level conclusion survives the preregistered multiplicity procedure.
Search provenance is sufficient to evaluate the selected model under the declared correction.
forbidden_escalations: single correction -> complete protection against data snooping

claim_classes.name: HISTORICAL POINT-IN-TIME CLAIM
claim_classes.definition: Claim that every materially influencing datum, feature, parameter, annotation, model choice, or transformation was admissible at the declared historical decision time under the declared research mode.
examples: The feature set was historically knowable at each decision timestamp.
The selected data vintage was the defensible vintage available at T.
forbidden_escalations: latest revised vintage -> historically available vintage

claim_classes.name: PATH-RISK / RUIN CLAIM
claim_classes.definition: Claim about path-dependent downside, tail loss, drawdown, survival, or risk of ruin under an exact declared policy and dependence-preserving path model.
examples: Estimated ruin probability under the exact policy is below the preregistered threshold.
Tail/path risk remains bounded under the declared dependence-preserving resampling model.

claim_classes.name: OOS / PRISTINE CONFIRMATION CLAIM
claim_classes.definition: Claim based on evidence that was pristine relative to calibration, validation, model selection, and prior exposure under the declared experiment design.
examples: The frozen strategy confirms the preregistered claim on pristine OOS data.
The holdout remained unconsumed until the authorized confirmation.
